text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it actually does. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand, not to add new features. This often means renaming confusing variables, breaking long functions into smaller ones, or removing duplicated blocks. By doing this regularly, you reduce "technical debt"—the hidden cost of messy code that makes future changes slow and risky. When your code is more readable, you and your teammates can spot bugs faster and work more efficiently. Think of it like tidying up your desk: the files are still the same, but you can find everything much quicker.
